title: Interest Accrual on Interest-Bearing Debts, Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery
content:
Interest in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** accrues only on debt types whose annual interest rate is above zero; compensation, pension and education overpayments never bear interest.

On an interest-bearing debt:

- interest starts once the debt type's interest start period, in calendar days, has passed after the notice date without payment in full;
- each month adds simple interest at one twelfth of the annual rate on the balance at the start of that month, rounded to the cent;
- no interest accrues for a month in which the debt is on hold, or in a repayment plan that is current.

A month's interest is booked as an addition to the balance, dated the last day of the accrual month.

## Month-by-month test

| Month's situation | Interest for that month |
|---|---|
| Start period not yet passed | None |
| Start period passed, debt active, not paid in full | One twelfth of the annual rate on the start-of-month balance, rounded to the cent |
| Debt on hold that month | None |
| Debt in a repayment plan that is current that month | None |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

An interest-bearing debt at a hypothetical annual rate of 4.00 percent has a start-of-month balance of 7,250.50 USD. One month's interest is 7,250.50 multiplied by 4.00 percent and divided by twelve, that is 24.1683 USD, rounded to the cent: 24.17 USD. The next month's interest is figured on that next month's start-of-month balance, without compounding within the month.
